$comment: Plan-correctness eval. Each case is a question, the role asking it, and the function the planner should choose (null = no data call). This file is per-deployment: replace these examples with questions your own users actually ask, one batch per function. Run against a real model; CI uses a stub so builds stay deterministic. Track the score as functions are added — a drop usually means two descriptions have grown too similar.
$howToUse: 1. Add 5-10 questions per live function, in the words your users use.
2. Include boundary cases: pairs of questions that differ only in which function is right.
3. Include negatives (expect: null) — small talk, and things you do not support.
4. Re-run after every batch of new functions.

cases.question: what's the status of order ORD-10023
list open orders for this month
how many orders are still unshipped

cases.$comment: Boundary pair — one order versus many. This is where confusable descriptions show up first.
cases.question: is order ORD-10023 shipped

cases.$comment: Write. The planner should choose the action, not the lookup, when the user is asking for a change.
cases.question: cancel order 10023

cases.$comment: Role boundary — the same question from a role that may not call the function should produce no plan.
cases.question: cancel order 10023

cases.$comment: ── Negatives. Every eval set needs these. ──
cases.question: hello
write me a poem about logistics
